citation.authors: Papandreou D, Magriplis E, Abboud M et al.
citation.title: Consumption of Raw Orange, 100% Fresh Orange Juice, and Nectar- Sweetened Orange Juice—Effects on Blood Glucose and Insulin Levels on Healthy Subjects

reported.what: serum insulin at 0, 30, 60, 90, 120 min after raw oranges, fresh juice and nectar-sweetened juice, mean (SD), n=20; Table 3 and Table 2 give no unit for insulin

serum glucose at the same times, mean (SD), n=20; Table 3 and Table 2 give no unit for glucose; the Methods print mmol/L for glucose only in the HOMA-IR formula (whereas the numbers are about 85) and mg/dL only for the 15 mg/dL difference of the sample-size calculation
fasting glucose and insulin by product, mean (SD), no unit

detail: Neither the glucose nor the insulin column of Tables 2 and 3 carries a unit, and no caption, footnote or figure legend supplies one. The Methods name glucose in mmol/L (HOMA-IR formula, which contradicts values near 85) and, separately, in mg/dL (the 15 mg/dL difference in the power calculation, not a unit of the results); insulin appears only as uU/mL inside the HOMA-IR formula, which does not reproduce the tabulated HOMA-IR from the tabulated insulin and glucose. The paper never ties a unit to the tabulated values, so none is supplied. The meals' carbohydrate, protein and fat grams are also not printed (Table 1 gives only total sugars), so no meal arm could be written either.
